activities.title: Temperature: molecules jiggle faster when hotter
Conduction: heat travels atom by atom
Radiation: hotter means more packets, faster
Misconception: a common mistake about heat and temperature

assessmentPoints: Average kinetic energy answers in the temperature activity
Trap answers in the misconception activity
successCriteria: The average kinetic energy doubles, but the speeds stay spread out and some molecules are still slow
average KE = (3/2) k T = 1.5 x 1.38 x 10^-23 x 300 = 6.21 x 10^-21 J at 300 K, doubling to 1.24 x 10^-20 J at 600 K
objectives.text: State that temperature is proportional to the average kinetic energy of the molecules, and calculate average KE = (3/2) k T

assessmentPoints: Gas law answers in the misconception activity
successCriteria: The pressure grows by a factor of 450 / 300 = 1.5, because at fixed volume p is proportional to the kelvin temperature: hotter molecules collide with the walls harder and more often.
objectives.text: Use the ideal-gas law pV = nRT and the fixed-volume rule p proportional to T, always in kelvin

assessmentPoints: Conduction answers in the conduction activity
Convection and radiation answers in the convection and radiation activities
successCriteria: Atoms at the hot end vibrate with larger amplitude and collide with their neighbours, passing kinetic energy along atom by atom through the lattice; in a metal, free electrons also carry energy rapidly through the rod. No atoms travel the length of the rod - the energy is relayed, and the far end warms as its atoms gain kinetic energy.
It expands, becomes less dense than the cooler water, and is pushed up
objectives.text: Distinguish conduction, convection and radiation, and explain each one at the particle level
